problem:
The diameter of the kibble of a particular cat food brand is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu $ and a standard deviation of $0.7\,\text{mm}.$ Additionally, the diameter of $20%$ of kibbles is less than $4.4\,\text{mm}$ in diameter. Find the percentage of kibbles whose diameter is less than $4\,\text{mm},$ rounded to $1$ decimal place.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.10\,$ | $\,0.15\,$ | $\,0.20\,$ | $\,0.25\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ | $\,-1.8808\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-1.0364\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.4\,$ | $\,0.0808\,$ | $\,0.0793\,$ | $\,0.0778\,$ |
| $\,-1.3\,$ | $\,0.0968\,$ | $\,0.0951\,$ | $\,0.0934\,$ |
| $\,-1.2\,$ | $\,0.1151\,$ | $\,0.1131\,$ | $\,0.1112\,$ |
worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the diameter of a randomly selected kibble. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{0.7}^{2}),$ and we want to find the $P(X<4).$

We know that $P(X<4.4)=0.20.$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4.4) & =0.20 \\ P(Z<\frac{4.4-\mu }{0.7}) & =0.20 \\ Φ(\frac{4.4-\mu }{0.7}) & =0.20 \\ \frac{4.4-\mu }{0.7} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.20)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.20)≈-0.8416.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4.4-\mu }{0.7} & =-0.8416 \\ 4.4-\mu  & =-0.58912 \\ \mu  & =4.98912\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X<4)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4) & =P(X\le 4) \\  & =P(Z\le \frac{4-4.98912}{0.7}) \\  & ≈P(Z\le -1.41) \\  & =0.0793 \\  & ≈7.9%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $7.9%$ of kibbles are less than $4\,\text{mm}$ in diameter.
